questions.q: What happens if you completely ignore a traffic ticket — neither paying nor filing an objection?
options: There is no consequence at all
The fine becomes final and can be collected through enforcement proceedings
You automatically receive a summons to trial
The fine is cancelled after a year
questions.explain: Ignoring a notice of a decision to impose a fine does not cancel it — it becomes final and can be enforced.

questions.q: Within how long of receiving the notice must you pay an administrative fine, if you do not file an objection?
options: A year
There is no fixed deadline
{{fact:enforcement.violation.payment_days}}
7 days
questions.explain: Under the Administrative Traffic Violations Law, you must pay within {{fact:enforcement.violation.payment_days}} from the day the notice was served, unless an objection or appeal is filed.

questions.q: Within how long can you file an objection to a decision to impose a fine?
options: A year
{{fact:enforcement.violation.objection_days}}
There is no time limit
One day
questions.explain: You must file an objection within {{fact:enforcement.violation.objection_days}} from the day the notice was served.

questions.q: What is the main difference between an administrative traffic violation and a criminal traffic offence?
options: A criminal offence is always cheaper
An administrative violation ends in a fixed fine with no trial; a criminal offence is handled by an indictment in court
There is no difference, both are handled the same way
An administrative violation applies only to new drivers
questions.explain: Most traffic offences are administrative violations with a fixed fine; serious offences (such as drink driving or causing death) are criminal offences with an indictment and a court hearing.

questions.q: Who decides whether a particular offence is handled on the administrative track or the criminal track?
options: The court decides in every case, before it is known which offence was committed
The law — the type of track is fixed in advance for each offence
The police officer on the spot, depending on their mood
The driver, according to their request
questions.explain: The type of track (administrative or criminal) is fixed in advance by law for each offence, and is not left to the officer's discretion on the spot.

questions.q: What is the fine for holding or using a handheld mobile phone without hands-free while driving?
options: A verbal warning only
{{fine:wheel-two-hands}} only, with no points
{{fine:phone-handheld}}, and {{points:phone-handheld}} points
Automatic disqualification for six months, with no fine
questions.explain: The offence carries a fine of {{fine:phone-handheld}} and {{points:phone-handheld}} points.

questions.q: What is the fine for driving without a seatbelt fastened (the driver themselves)?
options: No fine, just a note on the licence
{{fine:seatbelt-passenger}} only
{{fine:seatbelt-driver}}, and {{points:seatbelt-driver}} points
Immediate disqualification, with no fine
questions.explain: Not wearing a seatbelt as the driver carries a fine of {{fine:seatbelt-driver}} and {{points:seatbelt-driver}} points.

questions.q: How does the fine for carrying a child under 3 without a suitable child seat compare with the fine for driving through a red light?
options: The two fines are exactly the same
There is no fine at all for carrying a child without a seat
The fine for the child is higher: {{fine:child-under-3-no-seat}} compared with {{fine:red-light-main}}
The fine for a red light is higher: {{fine:red-light-main}} compared with {{fine:child-under-3-no-seat}}
questions.explain: The fine for driving through a red light ({{fine:red-light-main}}) is higher than the fine for carrying a child under 3 without a child seat ({{fine:child-under-3-no-seat}}), even though both offences are equally dangerous.

questions.q: Speeding by 35 km/h over the limit on an urban road — what can happen in addition to the fine and the points?
options: Nothing further can happen
The licence is automatically disqualified for a year
You must retake the theory test that same day
A police officer has the discretion to disqualify the licence immediately, for up to {{fact:police.suspension.offence_days}}
questions.explain: For a speeding excess of 31 to 40 km/h on an urban road, a police officer has the discretion to disqualify the licence immediately for up to {{fact:police.suspension.offence_days}}, in addition to the fine and the points.

questions.q: What is the fine for not letting a pedestrian finish crossing at a pedestrian crossing?
options: No fine, just a warning
{{fine:crosswalk-vehicle-stopped}} only
Disqualification with no fine
{{fine:pedestrian-crossing}}, and {{points:pedestrian-crossing}} points
questions.explain: Not letting a pedestrian finish crossing safely carries a fine of {{fine:pedestrian-crossing}} and {{points:pedestrian-crossing}} points.

questions.q: A driver is convicted of several offences included in a single indictment. How many points are recorded against them?
options: Zero points, since it is one indictment and not several tickets
One symbolic point per indictment
The sum of the points for all the offences together
Only the points for the most serious of the offences
questions.explain: Regulation 546 provides that when convicted of several offences in one indictment, only the points for the offence with the highest point count are recorded.

questions.q: News of a conviction reaches the Licensing Authority {{fact:points.registry-lag}} after the date of the conviction. What happens?
options: Only half the points are recorded
The driver is penalised with double points because of the delay
The points are recorded as usual
The points are not recorded at all
questions.explain: Information that reaches the Licensing Authority {{fact:points.registry-lag}} or more after the date of the conviction is not recorded as points on the register.

questions.q: A driver has accumulated {{fact:points.basic-course|n}} valid points. What applies to them?
options: No consequence until {{fact:points.advanced-course}}
A compulsory basic "Correct Driving" course with a test at the end
Immediate licence disqualification
A compulsory advanced course only
questions.explain: From {{fact:points.basic-course|n}} valid points up to below {{fact:points.advanced-course|n}}, the basic course is required; the advanced course ({{fact:points.advanced-course}} or more) comes only after passing the basic one.

questions.q: What is the difference between disqualification for {{fact:points.disqualification-3m}} and disqualification for {{fact:points.disqualification-9m}}?
options: Both are disqualification for life
The first is disqualification for {{fact:points.disqualification-3m.period}}; the second is for {{fact:points.disqualification-9m.period}}, with renewal only after medical checks and re-examination
There is no difference, they are identical
The first is more severe than the second
questions.explain: {{fact:points.disqualification-3m|n}} valid points — disqualification for {{fact:points.disqualification-3m.period}}. {{fact:points.disqualification-9m}}, or a repeat disqualification within {{fact:points.repeat_disqualification_window}} — disqualification for {{fact:points.disqualification-9m.period}}, with renewal only after medical checks and re-examination.

questions.q: A driver misses more than {{fact:points.course.max_absence}} of the hours of the "Correct Driving" course they were required to take. What is the result?
options: No consequence, as long as they attended most of the sessions
They receive a discount on a future fine
They are treated as not having completed the corrective measure
They automatically receive confirmation of completing the course
questions.explain: Regulation 551 provides that missing more than {{fact:points.course.max_absence}} of the course hours, or failing the closing test three times, counts as not completing the corrective measure.

questions.q: A driver is convicted of driving without compulsory insurance. What is the minimum disqualification the court may impose?
options: There is no disqualification for this offence
3 months
{{fact:insurance.no_insurance.min_disqualification}}, subject to the court's discretion to shorten it in special circumstances
Disqualification for life only
questions.explain: Driving without valid compulsory insurance can lead to a licence disqualification of at least {{fact:insurance.no_insurance.min_disqualification}}, unless the court finds special circumstances to shorten it.

questions.q: What allows a police officer to disqualify a driving licence immediately, even before a trial?
options: Reasonable grounds to believe the driver committed an offence from the Fourth Schedule to the Ordinance, or that an accident with a casualty occurred because of them
Only if the driver admits to the offence
Only for a parking offence
Any traffic offence, minor or serious
questions.explain: Section 47 of the Traffic Ordinance allows a police officer to take away a driving licence when there are reasonable grounds for an offence from the Fourth Schedule, or when the driver's offence caused an accident with a casualty.

questions.q: What is the disqualification period a police officer of rank may impose for an offence that caused a fatal road accident?
options: No disqualification, only a summons to trial
7 days
24 hours
{{fact:police.suspension.fatal_accident_days}}
questions.explain: For an offence that caused an accident in which a person was killed, a police officer of rank will disqualify the driver for {{fact:police.suspension.fatal_accident_days}}.

questions.q: A driver is disqualified by a police officer of rank. {{fact:police.suspension.void_no_indictment_months}} pass and no indictment has been filed against them. What happens to the disqualification?
options: It is cancelled automatically, unless the court orders otherwise
This has no effect on the disqualification at all
It automatically becomes a court disqualification
It remains in effect for life
questions.explain: If no indictment is filed within {{fact:police.suspension.void_no_indictment_months}} of the disqualification, it is cancelled automatically, unless the court orders, for special reasons, that it be extended.

questions.q: What is the difference between an expired driving licence and a disqualified driving licence?
options: An expired licence is an administrative matter that can be renewed; disqualification is an active ban on use, even with a valid licence
Disqualification is less severe than expiry
An expired licence is always more severe than disqualification
There is no practical difference
questions.explain: An expired licence can be renewed by paying a fee; disqualification bans use of the licence even if it is physically valid, and driving while disqualified is a serious offence in its own right.

questions.q: What is the correct action when you see a police officer signalling you to stop?
options: Ignore it if you have not committed an offence
Stop in the middle of the lane immediately, regardless of safety
Slow down, move right and stop in a safe place
Speed up and drive away
questions.explain: You must slow down, move right and stop in a safe place when signalled to stop — ignoring it or speeding up only makes things worse.

questions.q: What must a police officer do before requiring a driver to give a breath sample for a drink-driving test?
options: Explain the purpose of the test, ask for the driver's consent, and make clear the legal meaning of refusal
Obtain a court order in advance
Nothing, they may require it directly with no explanation
Wait 24 hours before the test
questions.explain: Section 64B of the Ordinance requires the officer to explain the purpose of the sample, ask for consent and explain the meaning of refusal, before requiring the sample.

questions.q: A driver refuses to give a breath sample for a drink-driving test. What is the legal meaning of this?
options: They receive a warning only, the first time
There is no consequence at all, since no test was actually carried out
They are treated as if they had committed the drink-driving offence itself
They must return to the station a week later
questions.explain: Section 64D of the Ordinance provides that refusing to give a sample is treated as if the driver had committed the drink-driving offence itself.

questions.q: For how long at most can someone who is not a suspect be detained for a drink-driving test?
options: 24 hours
There is no time limit
{{fact:alcohol.detention_non_suspect}}
5 minutes
questions.explain: Someone who is not a suspect can be detained for a drink-driving test for {{fact:alcohol.detention_non_suspect}} at most.

questions.q: A police officer not in uniform approaches a driver and asks for documents. What must the officer do first?
options: Call for an additional patrol car
Identify themselves with a warrant card
They have no duty at all, the request is valid immediately
Wait for the driver to ask for identification
questions.explain: A police officer not in uniform must identify themselves with a warrant card before giving instructions or requiring documents; an officer in uniform does not have to identify themselves separately.
